subject: Token accounting discrepancy & pilot packaging proposal
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@acme.ai>

Cc: procurement@acme.ai, ops@acme.ai
Date: 2027-03-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discrepancy on March invoice — token counts and emojis

Hi Kimberly,

We took a look at our March invoice and have a ~22% mismatch between the token counts on our side and what was billed. Our integration is long-lived streaming (chat session heartbeats + user messages) and we noticed a couple of patterns that might explain it: heavy emoji usage (frequent thumbs-ups), repeated prefix prompts that should be cached by your runtime, and a handful of very long single requests that stream over 60s.

I've attached the invoice and a small sample of our server logs showing the requests and timestamps (acme_sample_logs.json). Can you help us understand how Redwood is accounting for streaming partial tokens, long-context sessions, and reuse of KV cache across requests? We need this for our internal finance reconciliation and to decide whether to proceed with the annual pilot bundle we discussed.

We'd also like to discuss a temporary hold on payments for the disputed portion while this is investigated. Can you advise next steps and timelines?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Engineering, Acme.AI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March invoice — token counts and emojis

Hi Jordan — thanks for the note and attachments. Sorry for the upstream headache; we'll get this triaged today.

Quick answers up front while Tessa does a deeper look:
- Billing unit rounding: Redwood aggregates billable usage across the conversation window and applies tokenization-based rounding. Streaming fragments can result in fractional tokenization internally, but billing applies our per-request aggregation rules (we'll surface specifics below) rather than billing every socket fragment separately.
- KV/cache reuse: repeated identical prefixes within the same session are recognized for KV reuse; reused key-value entries reduce compute and should often avoid re-billing the same full prompt multiple times — however, there are edge cases where slightly different whitespace/emoji sequences break exact-match reuse.
- Emoji handling: emoji are tokenized (sometimes multiple subtokens) and can change counts significantly for high-volume emoji traffic.

Tessa — can you review the attached logs and confirm which of these mechanisms applied here and whether the invoice appears to have a calculation error? I've put procurement on CC to sync on any payment hold.

Best,
Kimberly
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March invoice — token counts and emojis

On 2027-03-21 09:12, Jordan Lee wrote:
> We took a look at our March invoice and have a ~22% mismatch...

I pulled the sample logs and matched them to our ingestion records. Summary of findings:
- Invoice math is consistent with our current metering policy, but two usage patterns amplify billed tokens: long single-turn streams with incremental partial-tokenization, and high-rate heartbeat messages with emoji.
- Metering specifics in play for this account: we aggregate tokens per conversation window (default 30 minutes of inactivity closes the window). Within a window we perform tokenization and compute billable tokens to 1 decimal place for internal accounting, then apply our billing quantum of 0.25 tokens when generating invoice line items. That means fractional subtokens get rounded up to the next 0.25 increment during invoice generation.
- KV cache reuse: across requests in the same live session we do a best-effort match for byte-equal prefixes. If a prefix differs (emoji or whitespace), it won't count as reuse. Where cache reuse is detected we apply a reduced compute multiplier; this shows up as reduced billed tokens for those requests but isn't guaranteed unless the prefix matches exactly.

Two anomalies I want to flag for investigation:
1) Your logs show a pattern of a tiny (<=5 byte) trailing whitespace variant after the prefix which would prevent exact-match reuse; if those are accidental (client-side), they would cause re-tokenization.
2) A handful of streaming requests appear to have been closed and re-opened within the same user action (likely due to a retry); we treat each closed request as a new request for metering purposes which can increase counts.

Recommended next step: if Acme can share a 24-hour dense sample (we have what you attached, but more dense traces around peak periods help), we can run a replay against our metering engine and produce a line-by-line billability trace. That will show exactly where the 22% difference arises.

Triage ETA: I can run the replay and produce a billability trace by EOD tomorrow if we get the denser logs.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Billing Operations, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redwood_billing_playbook.pdf - billing quantum & windowing reference)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March invoice — token counts and emojis

Thanks for flagging. Quick internal notes and a proposal:
- Confirming Tessa's description: our invoice generator applies a 0.25-token quantum for consumer-visible invoice lines; the metering engine tracks at finer granularity internally. Streaming fragments and retries inflate counts when requests are split or slightly mutated by the client.
- For this case I recommend a two-part resolution: (1) one-time invoice adjustment equal to the portion we can trace to client-side retries/whitespace noise (I estimate ~28% of the disputed amount after replay), and (2) a packaging concession for the pilot: convert Acme's upcoming quarterly pilot to a committed monthly bundle with a 12-month renewal at a 15% committed discount (instead of the 10% we discussed).
- Rationale: the committed bundle reduces the impact of per-request rounding because we amortize the quantum over higher volume and get more predictable unit economics; we also provide engineering guidance on client-side normalization to avoid whitespace/emoji churn.

If legal signs off on the concession I can approve the one-time credit up to $18,500 and the 15% committed discount for a 12-month signed agreement. Vanessa, can you handle commercial outreach and do we need to route this through revenue ops for approval?

Rishi
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Subject: Proposal & next steps — Acme reconciliation and pilot packaging

Jordan — thanks for your patience. Actionable next steps below: 

1) Invoice adjustment: we will run the replay once you provide a denser 24-hour sample. Based on our preliminary pass (and subject to final replay), Redwood will issue a one-time credit estimated at $18,500 to be applied to your April invoice. If final replay changes the number we'll update the adjustment accordingly, but we will not ask you to pay the disputed portion while we complete the replay.

2) Pilot packaging option (recommended): convert the previously proposed trial into a committed monthly bundle (50k tokens/month) with an annual renewal and a 15% committed discount. Benefits: predictable unit economics, amortized rounding, and priority support for billing and KV-cache tuning.

3) Mutual action plan: attached is a short MAP (acme_map.xlsx) that outlines deliverables, milestones, and timelines. Please review, sign, and return. I've also included a DocuSign link for the commitment so procurement can accelerate (links above).

Requested items from Acme: the denser log sample (24-hour window covering a peak), confirmation from procurement on whether they need PO or SOW, and the name/email for the legal contact to route the revised terms.

I'll schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the MAP and replay plan; Vanessa will follow up with commercial terms and a DocuSign package.

Best,
